message.content:
The three most significant schisms in Christian history are:

| # | Schism | Approximate Date | Key Parties Involved | Main Cause(s) |
|---|--------|------------------|----------------------|---------------|
| 1 | **Great Schism (East–West Schism)** | 1054 CE | Eastern Orthodox Church vs. Roman Catholic Church | Doctrinal differences (e.g., Filioque clause, papal primacy), cultural and political tensions between the Byzantine East and Latin West. |
| 2 | **Protestant Reformation** | 1517–1648 CE | Various Protestant movements (Lutheran, Calvinist, Anglican, etc.) vs. Roman Catholic Church | Accusations of corruption, doctrinal disputes (e.g., justification by faith, authority of Scripture vs. tradition), economic and political factors. |
| 3 | **East–West Schism of 1965 (also called the 1965 Schism)** | 1965 CE | Eastern Orthodox Church vs. Roman Catholic Church (in the context of the Second Vatican Council and modern ecumenical efforts) | Continued theological and ecclesiological disagreements, especially regarding the nature of the Holy Spirit, the role of the Pope, and liturgical practices. |

These three events represent the most profound and lasting divisions within Christianity, each reshaping the religious, cultural, and political landscapes of their times.
